description: The echo effect of the S-SMP chip from the Super Nintendo, a stereo delay whose feedback path runs through an eight tap filter

params.text: Sets the delay time in sixteen steps of 16ms, from nothing up to a quarter of a second
Sets how much of the delayed signal is fed back into the delay, -128 to 127; negative settings feed it back inverted
Sets how much of the delayed signal is mixed into that output, -128 to 127, with 0 giving the dry signal alone
Sets that tap of the eight tap filter in the feedback path, -128 to 127; the first tap alone at full and the rest at zero is a flat response
Attenuates the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to that filter tap, and inverts it below zero
Sets the gain applied to that input before it reaches the chip, up to 6dB
Passes the input straight to the output with the echo taken out of the path

inputs.text: Right signal to be echoed; unpatched it reads the left input
Moves the delay time, 10V spanning all sixteen steps
Moves the feedback amount, 10V spanning the whole knob range
Moves the left echo mix, 10V spanning the whole knob range
Moves the right echo mix, 10V spanning the whole knob range; unpatched it reads the left mix jack
Moves that filter tap through its own attenuverter, 10V spanning the whole slider range; unpatched it reads the tap jack above it, and the first tap reads 0V

outputs.text: Carries that side of the echoed signal

notes: the eight sliders are one filter across the delay's feedback path, numbered 1 to 8 down the panel; leaving the first at its full setting and the rest at zero passes the echo through unaltered
the module ships with a folder of presets named after the games whose echo settings they reproduce, reachable from the preset item on the panel menu
